regions.name: European Russia West
visual_identifiers: older road infrastructure with potholes common
onion dome church architecture visible in towns

state_distinguishers.Moscow_Oblast: More developed infrastructure, Moscow Ring Road (MKAD) nearby, denser population, better road quality than other oblasts
state_distinguishers.Leningrad_Oblast: Near St Petersburg, more Scandinavian feel in some areas, specific Finnish-influenced architecture in northwest corners
state_distinguishers.Rural_oblasts: Very similar to each other, distinguish by road signs showing city names

regions.route_sign_clues: Russian federal highways use M prefix (M1, M10 etc). Regional roads use A or R prefix. Signs are in Cyrillic.
regions.gemini_hint: Look for city names on road signs in Cyrillic — that is the most reliable state identifier. Moscow region has noticeably better road quality. St Petersburg area has more European architectural feel.
common_false_positives: Birch forests — appear across almost all of European Russia, not state-specific
Flat terrain — most of European Russia is flat

regions.name: Siberia West
visual_identifiers: vast flat steppe transitioning to taiga
extreme temperature infrastructure (thick utility poles, specific insulation)

state_distinguishers.Novosibirsk: Largest Siberian city, more urban infrastructure visible
state_distinguishers.Tyumen_Oblast: Oil wealth visible in better infrastructure, specific oil industry signage

regions.route_sign_clues: R-254 Irtysh Highway through Omsk/Novosibirsk. P-254, P-255 common in this region.
regions.gemini_hint: West Siberia is extremely flat with vast open spaces. Look for oil infrastructure near Tyumen. City name signs are the only reliable state identifier.
common_false_positives: Taiga forest — appears across all of Siberia
Flat terrain — most of West Siberia is extremely flat
Wooden houses — appear across all rural Russia

regions.name: Siberia East and Far East
visual_identifiers: more Asian influence in architecture near Chinese/Mongolian border
Primorsky has Pacific Ocean coastal feel
Sakha has permafrost infrastructure (houses on stilts)
taiga becomes more dramatic and hilly

state_distinguishers.Primorsky_Krai: Pacific coast feel, more Asian commercial signage influence, Vladivostok urban area distinctive
state_distinguishers.Buryatia: Buddhist temple architecture, Mongolian cultural influence visible
state_distinguishers.Sakha: Extreme cold infrastructure, houses on stilts over permafrost, very remote feel

regions.route_sign_clues: M58 Amur Highway in Far East. Very few paved roads in Sakha.
regions.gemini_hint: Buddhist temples or Mongolian architecture = likely Buryatia. Pacific coast urban feel = Primorsky/Vladivostok. Houses on stilts = Sakha permafrost zone.
common_false_positives: Mountainous taiga — hard to distinguish specific oblast from terrain alone

regions.name: Ural Region
visual_identifiers: mix of European and Asian Russia feel
heavy industrial signage in some areas

state_distinguishers.Bashkortostan: Islamic architecture visible in places, Ufa city distinctive

regions.route_sign_clues: M5 Ural Highway runs through Chelyabinsk. M7 Volga through Bashkortostan.
regions.gemini_hint: Ural mountains visible = Ural region confirmed. Islamic architecture or mosque = likely Bashkortostan. Heavy industrial = likely Chelyabinsk or Sverdlovsk.
common_false_positives: Industrial infrastructure — hard to distinguish specific oblast

regions.name: Southern Russia and Caucasus
visual_identifiers: Black Sea coastal infrastructure in Krasnodar
more colorful architecture than northern Russia

state_distinguishers.Krasnodar: Black Sea coast, resort feel, Sochi Olympic infrastructure, subtropical vegetation near coast
state_distinguishers.Dagestan: Islamic architecture, mountainous terrain, Arabic/local script alongside Cyrillic
state_distinguishers.Rostov: Flat Don steppe, agricultural plains, similar to Ukraine

regions.route_sign_clues: M4 Don Highway through Rostov/Krasnodar. Resort signage near Sochi.
regions.gemini_hint: Subtropical vegetation + Black Sea = Krasnodar near Sochi. Islamic architecture + Caucasus mountains = Dagestan or Chechnya. Flat sunflower fields = Rostov or Krasnodar steppe.
common_false_positives: Steppe terrain — shared with Ukraine and Kazakhstan
